definition: Protean means readily taking many different forms.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word protean. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know protean should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Clay is a protean material in the right hands — a bowl by morning, re-wetted and rolled into a bird whistle by dusk.
Changeable says only that change can happen — changeable weather — and stops short of protean.
Fluid goes further than changeable, moving smoothly from one state into the next, but it stops short of protean, which takes on form after fully different form.

Versatile praises range of use — a versatile tool or actor handles many different tasks well. Protean is stranger and grander: the thing itself keeps taking new forms, one after another, readily. A versatile cook masters many dishes; a protean talent seems to become a different cook each season.

Shape-shifting means changing bodily form, with a folklore flavor — wolves at the full moon, gods in disguise. Protean carries the same picture into ordinary praise: a protean actor or material takes on form after form, no magic required. Shape-shifting is literal transformation; protean is transformation as a talent.
holding the same form through everything
set firmly in one shape or position

Proteus lent his name to this one adjective and stopped; no other common English word is built on him. Protein looks like a cousin but is not — it comes from Greek protos, 'first,' a different root altogether. When a word's root is a single name, there is no family to find.
Protean means readily taking many different forms.

The influenza virus is protean: the coat of surface proteins it shows the immune system this winter will be subtly re-cut by next winter, and the antibodies that ended last year's infection may not recognize the new silhouette at all.
That is why the vaccine must be reformulated annually — the target will not hold one shape.

Protean is grander than 'changeable' because it promises whole new forms, one after another, taken readily — the word remembers Proteus, the sea god who flowed from lion to serpent to water in a wrestler's grip.
Changeable weather shifts within its usual range; a protean talent keeps arriving in shapes you have not seen.
Protean is a literary compliment — for actors, talents, materials, and imaginations that keep producing new forms.
Its unit-mate variegated is many colors on one surface at one moment; protean is many forms across time.
If you only mean 'adjusts well,' the plainer word is flexible.

For her linguistics project, Amara tracked a single slang word through six decades of student newspapers.
The word proved protean: in the 1960s it was a noun for a dance, by the 1980s a verb meaning to leave quickly, and by 2000 an adjective of vague approval.
Each decade did not just stretch the old meaning — it issued a genuinely new one, with new grammar to match.
Her professor warned that most slang simply fades, but this word kept re-emerging in a fresh form every time it seemed spent.
Amara's conclusion was cheerful: some words survive by holding their shape, and a few survive by refusing to keep any shape at all.
